text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- High court for fiscal cases smashes special tax tariff for foreigners. (p1)
- New research by central statistics office CBS links people's qualification with labour prospects. (p1)
- Agricultural minister Jozias van Aartsen and waste disposal company VAM disagree on sale of state-owned utility company Edon. (p3)
- Introduction of Dutch PTT Postbank's smart card, the chipper, slower than originally planned. (p3)
- Rabobank is to introduce a new code of conduct for mortgage lenders. (p11)
- Every step taken by agricultural minister to curb swine fever has been too late. (p1)
- Holland Media Group chiefs Boermans and Roemer dismissed for self-enrichment. (p1)
- Post and telecom company KPN should by split up into two separate units, according to U.S. bank Goldman Sachs and consultants McKinsey. (p2)
- Steering committee against car theft plans experiment with chips in vehicles to identify and trace them. (p1)
- Strike actions of council workers over pay continue. (p3)
- Philips Electronics president Cor Boonstra takes back much of his criticism of advertising agencies. (p33)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm fights for having circumscription "God be with us" on the euro. (p1)
